study_design: Prospective cohort study of cancer-free UK Biobank participants
cohort_total_n_excerpt: A total of 450,207 eligible participants (mean age: 56.2 years; females: 53.3%) were included, of whom 84,895 (18.9%) reported regular glucosamine use at baseline.
reason: The study prospectively evaluates incident site-specific cancers, including overall prostate cancer, but the abstract does not analyze high-grade, advanced, metastatic, lethal, or otherwise aggressive prostate cancer.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: During a median of 12.5 years follow-up, glucosamine use was significantly associated with an increased risk of overall cancer [HR, 1.04; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.01-1.06], skin cancer (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.07-1.15), and prostate cancer (HR, 1.07; 95% CI, 1.01-1.13), and with a reduced risk of lung cancer (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.79-0.97) after adjusting for potential confounders.
estimate_classifications.reason: The HR of 1.07 is explicitly reported for incident prostate cancer generally, without an aggressive subtype definition.
